chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, who said:

I asked him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), about a man who freed his concubine: is it permissible for him to marry her without a waiting period? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And for another man?' He said, 'No, until she observes a waiting period of three months.'

And when he buys her and frees her, it is preferable for him to observe her waiting period (istibra') before contracting marriage with her; and if he does not do so, there is no blame upon him. And we have previously mentioned this in the narration of Mansur ibn Hazim, and to add clarity to that, what he narrated:

key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَهَا: he observes her waiting period (to check for pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a man to marry the female slave he frees?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *iddah* (waiting period) and *istibra'* (verification of pregnancy) in the context of manumitting a concubine (*Umm Walad*). It establishes that while the owner may marry her immediately upon freeing her, others must observe a three-month period to ensure lineage purity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing doubt in paternity (*shubhat al-nasab*). The preference for *istibra'* even for the owner highlights the practical application of Quranic principles regarding marital purity and lineage verification.
